title: Cock and Ball Pressure — Solo
description: Testing what range of sensation the cock and balls respond to — from barely-touching to moderate pressure — builds a map most people have never deliberately made, and the range turns out to be broader than most people expect.
safetyNote: Build pressure gradually and stop if anything produces sharp or lasting pain. Avoid sudden impact on the testicles — pressure should be slow and deliberate throughout.

instructions.label: Solo
instructions.content: Set aside fifteen minutes with no goal of orgasm. Move to the shaft: try a light grip varying from barely-touching to firm, and sustained compression at different points along the length. You're mapping the range of sensation this anatomy produces outside goal-oriented stimulation — finding where different types of pressure register as interesting rather than merely uncomfortable or neutral.

instructions.label: With a partner
instructions.content: The natural extension is a partner applying the same range of pressure — which adds the dynamic element and allows the receiver to relax entirely rather than operating the stimulation themselves. That experience is covered in Partner CBT (Light).

explore: Is there a threshold where pressure shifts from neutral to interesting — and where does that threshold sit?
Does sustained compression produce a different sensation from increasing-and-releasing pressure?
Are there specific areas — the base of the shaft, particular areas of the testicles — that produce more response than others?
Does this change how you think about pressure and intensity in this area more broadly?
why: Most genital stimulation uses a narrow range of pressure in a specific rhythm aimed at a specific outcome. Systematic pressure exploration is different: you're testing the full range of what the anatomy responds to outside that narrow corridor. Many people discover that moderate testicular pressure produces a response they find genuinely interesting; others discover their response is clearly discomfort, which is equally useful. The solo version gives you exact control over the calibration without any need to communicate in real time — you learn the range before involving anyone else.
